questions: How many pupils are in the whole class, and how do you know?
What fraction chose apples, and what fraction chose grapes?
segments.say: Reading a pie chart: who likes what? Watch the twelve pupils gather into wedges: apples take half the pie, bananas and grapes a quarter each. Keep your student notes open at the pie chart definition for this scene.

questions: How many plants were sold in each month?
Where does the line dip, and is sales rising or falling overall?
segments.say: Reading a line graph: a rising trend. Follow the probe dot as it draws the line month to month: Jan 20, Feb 35, a small dip in March to 30, then April 50. Now try the line graph questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: How many votes did soccer and badminton each get?
How do we find how many more chose soccer?
segments.say: Worked example: comparing two bars of data. Watch the bars grow from the baseline, read the labels - soccer 13, badminton 8, swimming 3 - then follow the chip across the gap as we subtract: 13 - 8 = 5.

questions: Which shop looks like it rose faster?
What do the two axes tell us that the lines do not?
segments.say: Watch out: a steeper line is not always bigger. Both shops rose from 20 to 40, but graph B uses an axis of 0 to 200 so its line looks flatter. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this trap.
segments.watchFor: A steeper line always means a bigger increase. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the exit ticket: Steepness is judged by the drawing rather than the axis scale behind it. Send them back to scene s4 and to the correct turn: Slope depends on the axis scale: two graphs can have the same rise but look different.
